questions.prompt: Put the everyday Git loop in order.
questions.explanation: Change → check → stage → commit. You'll do this many times a day.

questions.prompt: Match the Git word to its case-history equivalent.
pairs: A case note saying what changed and why
Choosing what to attach before saving the note
questions.explanation: Git is a history of your project, one note (commit) at a time.

questions.prompt: Which is the best commit message?
questions.explanation: Say what the change does, so anyone reading the history understands it.

questions.prompt: You type `git commit -m "Add totals"` and Git says *nothing added to commit*. What did you forget?
options: `git add` to stage the file first
To save the file in Python
questions.explanation: Commit only saves what's been staged with `git add`.

questions.prompt: Which command shows what's changed since the last commit? `git ______`
questions.explanation: `git status` is your best friend. Run it whenever you're unsure.
